description: LINDA transparent scam-message heuristics. One rulebook shared by the in-browser scanner (TypeScript) and the backend (Python). Patterns use only syntax that behaves identically in JavaScript and Python regular expressions and are matched case-insensitively.

bands.label: Low risk
bands.summary: No strong scam signals found. That is not a guarantee the message is safe.

bands.label: Caution
bands.summary: Some warning signs. Verify with the sender through a channel you already trust.

bands.label: High risk
bands.summary: Several scam signals. Do not reply, click, pay or share codes.

bands.label: Very high risk
bands.summary: Matches common scam patterns closely. Treat it as a scam attempt.

rules.label: Asks you to share your PIN or password
rules.advice: Safaricom says its staff will never ask for your M-PESA PIN. Never share it with anyone.

rules.label: Asks you to share a one-time code
rules.advice: One-time codes are only for you. Anyone asking you to read one out is trying to take over an account.

rules.label: Says a PIN is needed to receive or reverse money
rules.advice: You never need a PIN to receive money. Only the sender enters a PIN.

rules.label: Claims money was sent to you by mistake
rules.advice: Check your real M-PESA balance first. Safaricom handles genuine reversals; do not send money back yourself because a stranger asks.

rules.label: Says you have won a prize or promotion
rules.advice: If you did not enter a promotion, you did not win one. Check promotions on the organisation's official channels.

rules.label: Asks for a fee before you can receive something
patterns: \b(ada ya|lipa ada|pay a fee|send ksh ?[0-9,]+ to (claim|receive|activate|unlock))\b
rules.advice: Real prizes, loans and jobs do not ask you to pay first.

rules.label: Pressures you to act fast
patterns: \b(urgent|urgently|immediately|today only|last chance|haraka|sasa hivi|mara moja|leo tu|within [0-9]+ ?(minutes|mins|hours|hrs)|kabla ya saa|expires? (today|soon|in))\b
rules.advice: Pressure to act now is a classic scam tactic. Slow down and verify.

rules.label: Threatens to block or suspend your account or line
rules.advice: Check your account status yourself through an official app or shop, not through a link or number in the message.

rules.label: Asks you to verify or update account details
rules.advice: Organisations do not ask you to verify accounts through links or numbers sent by SMS.

rules.label: Mentions a trusted brand
rules.advice: Scammers borrow trusted names. A brand name alone proves nothing about who sent the message.

rules.label: Claims to be customer care or staff
patterns: \b(customer care|customer service|customer support|huduma kwa wateja|calling from|kutoka safaricom|from safaricom)\b
rules.advice: Safaricom's published guidance says it calls customers from 0722 000 000. Hang up and call back through an official number.

rules.label: Asks you to pay a different number, till or account
patterns: \b(send|pay|deposit|tuma|lipa)\b[^.\n]{0,40}\b(to (this|my|the following|another|a new|our new) (number|till|paybill|account|line)|kwa (namba|nambari) hii|kwa till hii)\b
rules.advice: Confirm any change of payment details by calling the person or business on a number you already know.

rules.label: Offers a loan or limit increase
rules.advice: Check loan and Fuliza limits only in official apps or USSD menus you open yourself.

rules.label: Tells you to dial a code
rules.advice: Safaricom warns never to dial a code a caller or message gives you. Some codes can divert your calls or move money.

rules.label: Asks you to call or reply to a specific number
rules.advice: Call organisations back on numbers from their official website or the back of your card, not the one in the message.

rules.label: Asks you to keep it secret
patterns: \b(don't tell anyone|do not tell anyone|keep this (secret|confidential)|usimwambie mtu|usimwambie yeyote)\b
rules.advice: Requests for secrecy are designed to stop you from checking with someone you trust.

rules.label: Describes an emergency to get money
rules.advice: Call the person directly on their usual number before sending anything.

rules.label: Offers a job or recruitment
rules.advice: Genuine employers do not charge application, interview or uniform fees.

combos.label: Uses a trusted name and asks for a secret code
Mistaken-payment story with a request to pay or call
Claims to be official and asks you to dial a code
Link combined with an account warning
